X02.latin: Universum hoc, antiqui Musica contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil enim in rerum natura absque commensuratione et proportione consistit:

claude.sense: The ancients declared that this universe is held together by (or rests on) music. For nothing in the nature of things subsists without commensuration and proportion,

text_issues_review.printed: Vniuersum hoc, antiqui Musica contineri perhibuerunt (40.3–4)
text_issues_review.proposal: «Эта вселенная, как утверждали древние, заключена в музыке.» / 'This universe, the ancients declared, is contained in music.'
text_issues_review.why: Contineri with a bare ablative can mean 'be held together by' (L&S contineo I.B.1) or 'be contained in, consist in, rest upon' (L&S I.B.3.b, e.g. Cic. Fin. 2.48 'quattuor his virtutibus continetur'). The following argument (nothing subsists without proportion) favours 'held together', which all four chose; the alternative is grammatically sound and worth a note.
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. contineo, I.B.1 and I.B.3.b [checked]

best_ru.why: Exact and natural («эта вселенная держится музыкой»); B's «весь этот мир» slightly over-renders universum hoc.

best_en.why: Exact; C keeps the word order of the Latin, A is equally sound.

notes_to_keep.gist: Commensuratio is a late (Boethian) word, 'due measure, symmetry'; Xylander pairs it with proportio here and in X03 and with proportionalitas in X04; Vinet has symmetria.
Proportio later (X25 and after) is Xylander's Boethian word for the numerical ratio of an interval; the rendering 'proportion' keeps his word.

editor_questions: Musica contineri: keep 'held together by music' (all four) and record 'rests on / is contained in music' in a note?

sol.sense: The ancients maintained that music holds this universe together. Nothing in nature exists without due measure and proportion. The argument continues in X03.

text_issues_review.printed: VNiuersum hoc, antiqui Musica / contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil e- / nim in rerum natura absque com- / mensuratione et proportione con- / sistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ
text_issues_review.proposal: Эта вселенная, как утверждали древние, заключена в музыке. / This universe, the ancients declared, is contained in music.
text_issues_review.why: A bare ablative with contineor can be locative, as Allen and Greenough §431 specifically notes, so the grammar alone does not rule out ‘contained within music’. Here the following claim that due measure and proportion operate throughout nature and X07's account of music arranging all things support the stronger causal ‘held together by music’.
evidence: Allen and Greenough, New Latin Grammar, §§409 and 431 [checked]
Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. contineo A [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica I.2, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 187–189 [checked]

best_ru.why: The active construction conveys what holds the universe together.

best_en.why: Both preserve the cosmic claim and the two distinct measure terms.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain the sense of commensuratio and its coordination with proportio and proportionalitas.
Boethius, De institutione musica I.2, ed. Friedlein (1867), pp. 187–189 [checked] gives a precise parallel for cosmic music in the heavens, elements, and seasons.

astra.sense: The ancients said that music holds this universe together: nothing in nature subsists without commensuration and proportion.

text_issues_review.printed: VNiuersum hoc, antiqui Musica / contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil e- / nim in rerum natura absque com- / mensuratione et proportione con- / sistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ
text_issues_review.proposal: Эта вселенная, как утверждали древние, заключена в музыке. / This universe, the ancients declared, is contained in music.
text_issues_review.why: The bare ablative gives the means by which things hold together. X04 calls music the universe’s harmony and X07 describes it ordering all things. Spatial enclosure obscures that argument.

best_ru.why: The active construction makes the cosmic function of music immediately intelligible.

best_en.why: Preserves both members of the recurring pair and the opening emphasis on the universe.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep the lexical distinction between commensuratio, proportio and the proportionalitas of X04, especially ahead of the numerical use of proportio.

X03.latin: neque quicquam eorum quae fiunt, sine debita commensuratione et proportione si fiat, recte productum natumve esse dicitur: sive id ab arte efficiatur, sive a natura: et sive sub sensum illud cadat, sive solo intellectu perspiciatur.

claude.sense: and nothing that comes to be, if it comes to be without due commensuration and proportion, is said to have been rightly produced or born, whether it is brought about by art or by nature, and whether it falls under sense or is discerned by the intellect alone.

best_ru.why: Both keep the conditional si fiat and the plain dicitur («не называется», «не говорят»); B and D shift dicitur to a modal («нельзя назвать / нельзя сказать»).

best_en.why: Closest to the structure (neque ... si fiat ... dicitur) and fully idiomatic.

sol.sense: Nothing that comes about without due measure and proportion is said to have been properly produced or born, whether art or nature brings it about and whether sense or intellect alone apprehends it.

errors.quote: anything among the things that come to be said to have been

errors.fix: Set the condition off before the main predicate, as in C.

best_ru.why: The conditional and both pairs are clear.

best_en.why: Both keep the condition and the two independent pairs of alternatives.

X04.latin: Caeterum Musica ipsa per se commensuratio quaedam omnino et proportionalitas est, nimirum harmonia universi existens.

claude.sense: Music itself, in its own right, is altogether a kind of commensuration and proportionality, being namely (doubtless) the harmony of the universe.

The basic sense of omnino is 'altogether, wholly, entirely' (L&S I); the asseverative 'certainly, to be sure' is concessive and normally answered by sed or autem (L&S II.B), which is absent here. B and D are possible as an emphatic 'absolutely', but less natural; not an error.

X05.latin: Fortassis et ipsam divinam naturam haud inconvenienter sui ipsius et universi harmoniam quispiam dixerit: siquidem in Deo concinnatus, et ad consonantiam coaptatus mundus, bene, atque adeo quam optime se habere videtur.

claude.sense: Perhaps someone might not unfittingly call the divine nature itself the harmony of itself and of the universe, since the world, joined fitly together in God and fitted to consonance, is seen to be in a good, indeed the best possible, state.

best_ru.why: Keeps the potential subjunctive (назвал бы), the litotes in sense and the pair слаженный / прилаженный for concinnatus / coaptatus.

best_en.why: Both exact; A's 'framed' and C's 'attuned' for concinnatus are both defensible.

notes_to_keep.gist: concinnare ('to join fitly') and coaptare ('to fit together', ecclesiastical Latin) are Xylander's standing words for the fitting together of harmony (X12, X44–47, X56); haud inconvenienter is a litotes.
consonantia here is the concord of the cosmos, rendered 'consonance' by the project's rule; the text itself links cosmic harmony and musical consonance.

editor_questions: Consonantia in the cosmic sense (ad consonantiam coaptatus mundus): keep «консонанс» / 'consonance' by the convention, as all four do, or allow 'concord' here with a note?

Russian «напряжение голоса» risks being read as vocal strain; 'pitch / высота' is the modern-intelligible term (about.md §4.1). The choice must stay consistent through the version (cf. intensio et remissio = повышение и понижение).

(The Theon reference is not verified here.)

X16.latin: Quam enim rationem habet primus sonus ad octavum, eandem octavus ad decimumquintum obtinet.

best_en.why: Literal and clear.

sol.sense: The first note stands to the eighth in the same ratio as the eighth to the fifteenth. Each ascending span is an octave. The pitch multiplier is 2 in each case, 4 for the whole span. The frequency ratio in the order of the Latin is 1:2 for each span, and the inverse direction applies to string lengths at fixed tension and density.

errors.quote: 1st : 8th = octave, 2:1; 8th : 15th = octave, 2:1; 1st : 15th = 4:1
errors.problem: The checks write the lower note first but label each pair with the conventional higher-over-lower pitch ratio without identifying it as such. In the written order the frequency ratios are 1:2, 1:2 and 1:4. An ideal string-length interpretation would invert those.
errors.fix: State that the ascending pitch multipliers are 2, 2 and 4, and specify the order whenever assigning pitch or string-length ratios.

X18.latin: Intervallorum autem minimum genus est, quod diesin vocant: deinde semitonium, cuius dupla ad acutum est accessio, respectu dieseos. Deinde est tonus duplici constans semitonio, et rationem sesquioctavam constituens, ut est novenarii ad octonarium numerum. Quo fit, ut semitonium sit quasi dimidium sesquioctavae diesis autem quasi quadrans eiusdem.

claude.sense: The smallest kind of interval is the one they call the diesis; next the semitone, whose advance towards the high is double compared with the diesis. Next is the tone, consisting of two semitones and constituting the sesquioctave ratio [9:8], as of nine to eight. Hence the semitone is, as it were, half of the sesquioctave, and the diesis, as it were, a quarter of it.

Russian «род» is idiomatic for 'kind' and keeps genus apart from species, which the same translators render «вид» (X15, X26); B and D's «вид» merges the two Latin words. A legitimate choice either way, not an error.

best_ru.why: Exact; both keep quasi («как бы») and the bracket at both ratio names.

notes_to_keep.gist: The diesis is the quarter-tone; the magnitudes are Aristoxenian (tone = 2 semitones = 4 dieses), the tone is defined by the Pythagorean 9:8; quasi marks that half and quarter of 9:8 are not numerical ratios (argued in X19–25); dupla accessio is an ordinary 'double', no bracket.

Vinet here gives arithmetical numbers (8½ and 8¼ against 8, i.e. 17:16 and 33:32), Xylander a division made geometrical in X19–X20; cf. Boethius I.21 'diesis autem est semitonii dimidium' and I.16 (the tone not divisible into equal halves in numbers).

sol.sense: The smallest interval is a diesis. Next comes the semitone, whose rise is double that of a diesis, then the tone, made of two semitones and standing in the sesquioctave ratio 9:8. The semitone is as it were half of that ratio and the diesis as it were a quarter. If the interval is divided in exactly equal musical steps, the resulting ratios are (9/8)^(1/2) and (9/8)^(1/4), approximately 1.06066 and 1.02988.

errors.quote: and the diesis a quarter of it
errors.problem: The Latin repeats quasi for the diesis. The English allows the second subdivision to be read as unqualified.
errors.fix: and the diesis, as it were, a quarter of it

errors.quote: из двойного полутона / of a double semitone
errors.problem: The expression can suggest one recognized kind of semitone called a double semitone. The text uses ordinary doubling to give the composition of the tone.
errors.fix: из двух полутонов / of two semitones

errors.quote: neither is a ratio of whole numbers, hence the text's ‘quasi’
errors.problem: The arithmetic is correct if the musical interval is split into equal logarithmic steps. The specific causal claim about Xylander's quasi is not verified. The word qualifies the analogy to a half or a quarter, and the text never states this modern calculation.
errors.fix: Give the calculation conditionally and leave the force of quasi at ‘as it were’. Specify whole-number terms when contrasting Boethius's impossibility result with the subsequent geometric argument.

text_issues_review.printed: dimidium sesquioctauæ diesis autem (42.14)

best_ru.why: Preserves both occurrences of quasi and makes accessio intelligible in terms of pitch.

The rise is double in interval size, and both subdivisions are qualified by quasi.

editor_questions: Insert punctuation between the two quasi clauses in the reading text if the normalization permits it.

astra.sense: The diesis is the least interval. The semitone rises twice as far as the diesis, and the tone consists of two semitones in the sense explained here. The tone is sesquioctave, nine to eight. The semitone is as it were half, the diesis as it were a quarter, of that interval.

errors.quote: and the diesis a quarter of it
errors.problem: The text repeats quasi before quadrans. Coordination can carry the earlier qualifier across, but the explicit second qualification disappears.
errors.fix: “and the diesis, as it were, a quarter of it.”

errors.quote: geometrically, as X19–X20 require
errors.problem: The texts give the possibility of a geometrical division of a material magnitude. They do not specify a construction by mean proportionals. Equal pitch-interval divisions have the stated radical ratios, but the derivation should be conditional.
errors.fix: If the intervals are bisected into equal pitch spans, the factors are the stated square and fourth roots.

text_issues_review.printed: dimidium sesquioctauæ diesis autem (42.14)
text_issues_review.proposal: punctuate: dimidium sesquioctavae, diesis autem
text_issues_review.why: The page reads sesquioctavae diesis autem without punctuation. Diesis is the new nominative, and autem articulates the second limb; a comma makes the transmitted syntax immediately clear.

text_issues_review.printed: dupla ad acutum est accessio, respectu dieseos
text_issues_review.proposal: whose increase toward the high is double
text_issues_review.why: Accessio can describe approach or increase. Ad acutum sets its direction, and dupla measures how far the pitch rises relative to the diesis. Either sense works if it describes the size of the upward step.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. accessio I and II.B [checked]

best_ru.why: The upward movement and both occurrences of quasi and of the 9:8 ratio are clear.

best_en.why: Gives an unambiguous rise in pitch and distinguishes both qualified subdivisions.

notes_to_keep.gist: The doubling concerns interval size. Equal musical halves and quarters of a 9:8 tone would have ratios √(9/8) and ⁴√(9/8). Preserve both instances of quasi. The passage supplies no integer ratios for its subdivisions.

editor_questions: How far should the commentary identify an exact geometric division? Xylander asserts geometric divisibility but supplies no numerical mean here.

X19.latin: Quamvis enim ratione numeri unitas dividi non potest, utique tamen unitas quae in materia conspicitur, dividitur Geometrice.

claude.sense: For although by the reckoning of number unity cannot be divided, yet unity seen in matter is certainly divided geometrically.

best_ru.why: Exact, renders utique («безусловно») and the indicative dividitur.

best_en.why: Exact, including utique ('certainly').

notes_to_keep.gist: The excess of 9 over 8 is a unit; halving 9:8 in numbers gives 16:17:18 with 17:16 ≠ 18:17, so an exact half would require dividing the unit, possible only for a magnitude on the string; ratione numeri is not the term 'ratio'.

Theon of Smyrna: the unit is indivisible as number, the sensible one divisible; Theon denies that the tone can be halved exactly, Xylander's text affirms a geometrical division (Theon references not verified here).

sol.sense: In arithmetic, the unit cannot be divided. A unit discerned in material magnitude can nonetheless be divided geometrically.

divergences.latin: ratione numeri unitas dividi non potest

readings.construal: The unit is indivisible under the rules of number.

X21.latin: Geometriae enim est, semper a maiori recta minorem posse detrahere, semperque posse minori apponere maiorem. ex quo sequitur, ut quaelibet figura ad placitum possit cum augeri, tum diminui.

claude.sense: For it belongs to geometry always to be able to take a smaller straight line from a greater and always to add a greater to a smaller; from which it follows that any figure can at will be both increased and diminished.

best_ru.why: Keep Geometriae est ('геометрии свойственно') and cum … tum.

notes_to_keep.gist: Recta = recta linea; cf. Euclid, Elements I.3 (cutting off from the greater straight line one equal to the less).

sol.sense: Geometry can always subtract the lesser straight length from the greater and add the greater to the lesser. A figure can accordingly be enlarged or diminished at will.

best_ru.why: Отрезок прямой correctly gives the finite straight magnitude under discussion.

best_en.why: Shorter and longer are exact in the geometrical setting, and each semper is kept.

notes_to_keep.gist: Euclid's construction of removing the equivalent of a lesser straight line from a greater supplies the mathematical parallel. Euclid, Elements I.3 [checked].

astra.sense: Geometry permits a smaller straight line always to be subtracted from a larger, and a larger to be added to a smaller. Any figure can consequently be enlarged and diminished at will.

best_ru.why: Отрезок identifies what can be added and subtracted, a finite length of straight line.

best_en.why: ‘Shorter’ and ‘longer’ precisely express the two measured magnitudes.

notes_to_keep.gist: Euclid I.3 gives the corresponding construction: cut from the greater straight line a segment equal to the lesser.

sol.sense: Arithmetic cannot bisect a square number into two equal square numbers or double it and still have a square. Xylander illustrates this with sixteen, half of which is eight and double of which is thirty-two. Neither eight nor thirty-two is an integer square. Geometry can make both areas as squares. The transmitted Numerorum is syntactically awkward.

А для геометрии сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, [arithmetic] cannot divide a given square into equal squares, or produce its double. For among numbers sixteen, which is a square, it can neither part into two squares (for it is impossible arithmetically for eight to be a square, or to give the square root of that number), nor can it give another square that is its double (for it cannot be that the number thirty-two is a square). But for geometry this is not hard to do.

readings.construal: Uses the intended numeral with an understood singular number rather than reproducing the loose genitive on its own.

В геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.

For one cannot split the number sixteen, which is square, into two [equal] squares (in arithmetic eight cannot be a square, nor can a square root be given for that number), or double it to give another square (for thirty-two cannot be a square number). In geometry this is not difficult to do.

Геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, [arithmetic] cannot divide a proposed square into equal squares, or make it double. For it cannot split the number sixteen, which is a square, into two squares (for it is impossible for eight to be arithmetically a square, or to give the square root of that number), nor give another square double of it (for it cannot be that the number thirty-two is a square). But for geometry this is not difficult to do.

quotes.ru: Кроме того, арифметика не может ни разделить данный квадрат на равные квадраты, ни удвоить его. Таково, например, квадратное число шестнадцать. Арифметика не может ни разложить его на два квадрата (ведь невозможно, чтобы восемь было квадратом в арифметическом смысле или чтобы можно было указать квадратный корень этого числа), ни получить другой квадрат, удвоив шестнадцать (ведь число тридцать два не может быть квадратом). Геометрии же сделать это нетрудно.
quotes.en: Moreover, arithmetic cannot divide a given square into equal squares or double it. Take the number sixteen, which is a square. Arithmetic can neither resolve it into two squares (for eight cannot be a square in arithmetic, nor can one give a square root of that number) nor give its double as another square (for the number thirty-two cannot be a square). Geometry, however, finds no difficulty in doing this.

divergences.verdict: The singular relative leads to numerus as the implied term, and sixteen is what arithmetic tries to divide. A's construction makes the print's difficulty visible, but among numbers sixteen can sound like sixteen unspecified numbers. Translate the one numeral clearly and put the loose genitive and possible emendation in the commentary.

sol.sense: Taking the original side as the new diagonal gives a square of half the original area. Taking the original diagonal as the new side gives a square of twice the original area. For side s, the areas are s²/2 and 2s². The ending propositum dupli is irregular, though its result is fully determined by the construction.

readings.construal: The new square is twice the original.

divergences.verdict: A or C. The modern established terms descend from the common Latin names that Xylander cites (quarta, quinta, octava; English fourth, fifth, octave), so the established term belongs on them, and the Greek names need a literal rendering (A) or a transliteration (C), as about.md §4.1 allows where a name is explained; both explain their departure from §4.2 in a note. B's and D's Russian invert the historical relation (diatessaron becomes «кварта», quarta becomes «четвёртая») but stay intelligible; D's English follows the opposite strategy to its Russian without comment; B's English loses the Greek names and with them the content of the sentence (major error below). The choice between literal and transliterated Greek names must agree with X29–X30 and X35. Literal glosses added to transliterated names in the running text go in square brackets (about.md §4.6), or into a note, since X29 explains the names at once. If transliteration is chosen, the note should warn that Russian «диапазон» is also the everyday word for 'range'.

divergences.verdict: about.md § 4.1 asks that the explanation of a name stay readable: the established term and the literal rendering side by side, or an explanation in a note. A does this in the running text, and its solution fits the function of the Latin best: Xylander glosses the Greek names by the names current in his own Latin (octava, quarta, quinta), which are exactly the modern established terms. D does the reverse (established terms for the Greek names, Xylander's Latin ordinals literally): acceptable, but «две восьмых» / 'two eighths' reads as the fraction 2/8. B renders both sets by the established terms; this follows § 4.2 but turns the 'hoc est' gloss into a tautology, explained only in its notes, and it departs from B's own solution in X28 and X35, where the Latin ordinals are rendered literally («четвёртой», «восьмая»). C keeps transliterations in the running text, a departure from § 4.2 for which it gives its reason in its X28 note (to keep Xylander's double naming visible); but transliterations are not terms a modern reader understands (§ 4.1), and Russian «диапазон» is the everyday word for 'range'.

X32.latin: Inter paraphonum et antiphonum, hoc est assonans et obsonans, hoc differt, quod illud quidem consonat inaequali tempore, quando soni mutuas suas proportionalitates atque rationes aequalitate quadam leniter et concinne sibi invicem succedunt. Antiphonum autem est, cum simul eodem tempore acutum cum gravi consonat: ut cum octavus primo, undecimus quarto, duodecimus quinto, decimusquintus octavo aequaliter ascendit vel descendit in intensionibus remissionibusve, ita ut acutis graves, vel contra, respondeant proportionaliter.

claude.sense: Paraphonon and antiphonon, that is 'assonans' and 'obsonans', differ in this: the former is consonant at unequal (i.e. different) times, when the notes, in respect of their mutual proportionalities and ratios, succeed one another gently and harmoniously with a certain evenness. Antiphonon is when high and low are consonant together at the same moment: as when the 8th note with the 1st, the 11th with the 4th, the 12th with the 5th, the 15th with the 8th rises or falls equally in raisings or lowerings, so that low notes answer to high, or vice versa, proportionally. (All four example pairs are octaves.)

divergences.verdict: The pair repeats in Latin the etymological glosses of X31 (iuxta sonans, contra sonans), so the prefixes carry the meaning: ad- for παρα-, ob- for ἀντι-. A and C render it so, and 'to sound to' is in fact the first gloss of assono in Lewis & Short. D follows the other attested sense of assono ('respond to', of Echo): lexically sound, but the paraphonic class then receives the notion of 'response' that the same segment attaches to antiphony ('acutis graves … respondeant'), and the contrast is weakened. B's Russian pair «вторящее / ответное» ('echoing / answering') is nearly synonymous, so the contrast vanishes; its English 'in accompaniment' is not a sense of assono, and 'in answer' is not a sense of obsono ('to interrupt by a sound'). A's Russian «звучащим при» is unidiomatic; C's calques are clear but are coinages and need the quotation marks and a note (about.md § 4.1).

C stays closest to the Latin; A's bracketed '[keeping]' is honest but adds a verb the Latin lacks; B and D are acceptable. Note that in the Boethian vocabulary proportionalitas is the 'proportion' (ἀναλογία) and ratio / proportio the 'ratio', so B's and D's 'proportions … ratios' is a defensible rendering of the pair; A's and C's 'proportionalities' is a literal calque.

sol.sense: Paraphony is consonance at different times, with an even and smooth succession of notes in mutual proportions and ratios. The two accusatives in this description have no clear governor. Antiphony is simultaneous consonance of high and low, illustrated by four parallel pairs a seven-step octave apart.

quotes.ru: Между парафонным и антифонным, то есть «звучащим при» и «звучащим навстречу», разница та, что первое консонирует в неравное время, когда звуки, [храня] взаимные свои пропорциональности и отношения, с некоторой равномерностью мягко и складно сменяют друг друга. Антифонное же — это когда высокое консонирует с низким вместе, в одно и то же время: например, когда восьмой [звук] с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым равномерно восходит или нисходит в повышениях или понижениях, так что низкие [звуки] высоким, или наоборот, отвечают пропорционально.
quotes.en: Between the paraphonon and the antiphonon, that is, the ‘sounding to’ and the ‘sounding over against’, the difference is this: the former is consonant at unequal time, when the notes, [keeping] their mutual proportionalities and ratios, succeed one another gently and neatly with a certain evenness. The antiphonon, on the other hand, is when high is consonant with low together, at the same time: as when the eighth [note] rises or falls evenly with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth, in raisings or lowerings, so that low [notes] answer to high, or the reverse, proportionally.

readings.construal: Treat the accusatives as the respect in which the succession has evenness, broadly equivalent to an implicit ‘according to’ or ‘in’.

quotes.ru: Парафония и антифония, то есть созвучие вторящее и ответное, различаются следующим. При парафонии звуки консонируют в разное время, когда они плавно и стройно следуют друг за другом, соблюдая некоторую равномерность во взаимных пропорциях и отношениях. Антифония же бывает, когда высокий звук консонирует с низким одновременно, как при равном повышении или понижении восьмого звука с первым, одиннадцатого с четвёртым, двенадцатого с пятым, пятнадцатого с восьмым, так что низкие звуки пропорционально отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony, that is, sounding in accompaniment and sounding in answer, differ as follows. In the former the notes are consonant at unequal times, succeeding one another smoothly and fittingly with a certain evenness in their mutual proportions and ratios. Antiphony occurs when a high note is consonant with a low one at the same time, as when the eighth and the first, the eleventh and the fourth, the twelfth and the fifth, and the fifteenth and the eighth rise or fall by equal changes in pitch, so that the low notes correspond proportionately to the high, or the reverse.

quotes.ru: Между парафонным и антифонным, то есть «призвучным» и «противозвучным», та разница, что первое консонирует в неодинаковое время, когда звуки по своим взаимным пропорциональностям и отношениям с некоторой равномерностью мягко и слаженно сменяют друг друга. Антифонное же — когда высокое консонирует с низким вместе, в одно и то же время: например, когда восьмой [звук] с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым одинаково поднимается или опускается в повышениях или понижениях, так что низкие пропорционально отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Between the paraphonon and the antiphonon, that is, the ‘sounding-to’ and the ‘sounding-against’, there is this difference: the former is consonant at unequal times, when the notes, in their mutual proportionalities and ratios, succeed one another gently and harmoniously with a certain evenness. The antiphonon is when the high is consonant with the low together, at the same time: as when the eighth [note] with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth rises or falls equally in raisings or lowerings, so that the low correspond proportionally to the high, or the reverse.

quotes.ru: Парафония и антифония, то есть «звучание в ответ» и «встречное звучание», различаются следующим образом. При первой звуки консонируют в разное время: соблюдая известную равномерность в своих взаимных пропорциях и отношениях, они плавно и стройно следуют друг за другом. Антифония же возникает, когда высокий звук консонирует с низким одновременно, в один и тот же миг. Так, при повышениях или понижениях восьмой звук поднимается или опускается наравне с первым, одиннадцатый — с четвёртым, двенадцатый — с пятым, пятнадцатый — с восьмым, и низкие звуки соразмерно отвечают высоким или наоборот.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony, that is, ‘sounding in response’ and ‘sounding opposite’, differ in this respect. In the former the notes are consonant at different times, succeeding one another smoothly and harmoniously with a certain evenness in their mutual proportions and ratios. Antiphony occurs when a high note is consonant with a low one at the very same time. Thus in raisings or lowerings [of pitch] the eighth rises or falls equally with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, and the fifteenth with the eighth, so that the low notes answer the high in due proportion, or conversely.

astra.sense: Paraphony and antiphony, glossed as sounding alongside and sounding opposite, differ in time. In the former the notes succeed one another smoothly and fittingly, with a certain evenness in their mutual proportions and ratios. In the latter high and low sound together. The eighth with the first, eleventh with fourth, twelfth with fifth and fifteenth with eighth ascend or descend alike as pitch is raised or lowered, low notes answering high proportionally or conversely.

X38.latin: Nam quia intervallum diapente diximus habere sesquialteram proportionem, equidem id non intelligendum est ad excessum quantitatis respiciendo, qua in respectu se praecedentium sonorum habet. Ea namque ratione ad primum esset quincuplum, ad secundum duplum sesquialterum: at tertio collatum, eum, eiusque bessem continet: sesquiquartum vero est ad quartum, nulli autem horum omnium sesquialtera proportione quadrat.

claude.sense: For when we said that the interval of the fifth has the sesquialter ratio, this is certainly not to be understood by looking at the excess of quantity, i.e. how it (the fifth note, the number 5) stands in relation to the notes preceding it. For on that reckoning it would be quintuple [5:1] to the first, duple sesquialter [5:2] to the second; compared with the third, it contains it and its two thirds (5:3); to the fourth it is sesquiquartan [5:4]; with none of all these does it fit in the sesquialter ratio.

При сопоставлении с третьим [пятый] заключает его в себе вместе с двумя его третями, а к четвёртому отношение сверхчетвертное [5:4]. Ни с одним из них полуторная [3:2] пропорция не получается.
quotes.en: For when we said that the fifth has a sesquialter [3:2] proportion, we certainly did not mean this in terms of its numerical excess over the notes that precede it. By that reckoning its ratio to the first would be quintuple [5:1] and to the second duple sesquialter [5:2]. Compared with the third it contains it and two thirds of it, and to the fourth it is sesquiquartan [5:4]. It stands in a sesquialter [3:2] proportion to none of them.

On that reckoning it would be quintuple [5:1] in relation to the first, duple sesquialter [5:2] in relation to the second. Compared with the third, it contains the third and two thirds of it. It is sesquiquartan [5:4] in relation to the fourth, and it stands in a sesquialter [3:2] ratio to none of them.

divergences.verdict: Amplitudo gives the magnitude or extent of the cavity without specifying a width as against another dimension. Spiritus here belongs to the blown instrument and the pair describes increasing and decreasing the effort or strength of breath, in contrast to string tensio. Theon explicitly mentions the breadth of cavities. The parallel explains the narrower possibility, while Xylander’s Latin word also permits the size of a cavity in general.

X42.latin: Porro systematum aliud est tetrachordum, quod quatuor componitur nervis, omnem vim intervalli diatessaron complectens: aliud pentachordum, quinque ex nervis constitutum, diapente intervalli omnem potestatem in se continens: aliud octachordum, octo ex nervis constructum, omnem octavae materiem ambiens. Est et quod continentibus sedecim nervis conficitur, omnem disdiapason (decimamquintam hodie vocant) intervalli ambitum comprehendens, eoque ad duplices usus habile, quod et praedicta intervalla, et ex his ipsis composita complectitur.

claude.sense: Further, of the systems one is the tetrachord, composed of four strings and embracing the whole force (vis) of the interval of the fourth; another the pentachord, made of five strings and containing in itself the whole power (potestas) of the interval of the fifth; another the octachord, built of eight strings and encompassing the whole matter (materies) of the octave. There is also one made of sixteen continuous strings, comprising the whole compass (ambitus) of the interval of the double octave (which today they call the fifteenth), and for that reason suited to twofold uses, because it embraces both the aforesaid intervals and those composed of them.

divergences.issue: Xylander's contemporary name for the double octave: literal 'fifteenth' or the established Russian term «квинтдецима»

readings.construal: Russian established term «квинтдецима»; English 'the fifteenth'

quotes.ru: (ныне её называют квинтдецимой)

quotes.ru: (ныне его называют пятнадцатой)
quotes.en: (today they call it the fifteenth)

divergences.verdict: Both are correct in sense. «Квинтдецима» is the established Russian name of the interval of two octaves (as нона, децима … квинтдецима), and so fits about.md § 4.1 and Xylander's point that this is the name current 'today'; English 'the fifteenth' is likewise the established English name. The literal «пятнадцатая» needs the quotation marks (B) to be readable; C's unmarked 'его называют пятнадцатой' is awkward.
divergences.recommended_ru: (ныне её называют квинтдецимой)

sol.sense: A tetrachord of four strings embraces the fourth, a pentachord of five the fifth and an octachord of eight the octave. A further system of sixteen consecutive strings encompasses the double octave, called the fifteenth in contemporary usage. It comprises both the named intervals and combinations of them.

errors.quote: the two octachords are counted separately
errors.problem: X15 expressly describes a sixteen-string structure on fifteen physical strings and reuses the last note as the beginning of the next series. X42 instead expressly says sixteen consecutive strings. The shared boundary offers a possible explanation, but the latter passage gives no separate count of two component octachords (Xylander 41.25–42.5 and 47.12–16 [checked]).
errors.fix: Give the two counts as written. Mention shared-endpoint counting as a possibility for the sixteen in this passage.

It serves two uses because it comprises the foregoing intervals and their compounds.

quotes.ru: Между системами, стало быть, и интервалами, заключёнными внутри них, различие то, что всякое устроение систем усматривается в материи, интервалы же мыслятся, когда материя отделена мыслью.

quotes.ru: Итак, между системами и интервалами, заключёнными внутри них, та разница, что всякое устроение систем рассматривается в материи, а интервалы постигаются, когда материя отделена мыслью.

quotes.ru: Итак, системы отличаются от заключённых в них интервалов тем, что всё устройство системы рассматривается в материи, а интервалы постигаются в отвлечении от материи.

quotes.en: The whole structure of a system is considered in matter, whereas intervals are grasped by abstracting from matter in thought.

divergences.verdict: Omnis with an abstract singular can emphasize entirety or extend a statement over all cases. Singular constitutio opposite the abstract consideration of intervals and the repeated omnem in X42 favour the collective sense.

text_issues_review.printed: in medio eorum concepta intervalla

text_issues_review.why: The mental sense is well motivated in a clause contrasting systems in matter with intervals known in thought.

best_ru.why: Joins the physical constitution to the act of mentally abstracting from matter.

X44.latin: Harmoniae proprium est, ut ea systemata construat atque concinnet ad horum melodiae (eam cantus seu cantilenae modulationem fere dixeris) generum aliquod, quae sunt diatonon, chromaticum, et harmonicum, cui ab ipsa Harmonia nomen obtigit.

claude.sense: It is proper to harmony to construct and fit together those systems according to some one of these genera of melody (which you might almost call the modulatio of song or cantilena): the diatonon, the chromatic and the harmonic, which last received its name from Harmony itself.

errors.quote: сообразно одному из родов мелодии / according to one of the genera of melody
errors.problem: 'horum' ('these', pointing forward to the list of genera) is left out.
errors.fix: сообразно одному из этих родов мелодии / according to one of these genera of melody

best_ru.why: Both complete and exact (horum, fere, the gloss on melodia, the name of the harmonic genus).

best_en.why: Exact, and 'measured shaping' avoids the modern sense of 'modulation' that C's English needs a note to exclude.

notes_to_keep.gist: The parenthesis is Xylander's gloss on the Greek word melodia; modulatio = measured, regulated singing (L&S, Quintilian); diatonon in Greek form, the other two in Latin form; 'harmonic' = the enharmonic genus, name kept by convention.
Diatonon (τὸ διάτονον) only here; Xylander writes diatonicum in X45, X48, X55; Boethius I.21 calls the third genus enarmonium.

editor_questions: modulatio (here and later): 'measured shaping' / «мерное ведение» (A), 'melodic movement' / «мелодическое движение» (B, C ru), 'modulation' (C en), «мелодический строй» (D)? To be fixed in the concordance with cantus, cantilena, melodia.

sol.sense: Harmony builds and fits its systems to one of three genera of melody. Melody can be termed the measured shaping of song or tune. The genera are diatonic, chromatic and harmonic, with the last taking its name from harmony itself.

divergences.latin: eam cantus seu cantilenae modulationem fere dixeris
divergences.issue: What modern musical sense does modulatio carry in the gloss on melody?

readings.construal: Measured shaping of song or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить и слаживать эти системы сообразно какому-либо из таких родов мелодии (её можно бы приблизительно назвать мерным ведением пения, или напева): диатонического, хроматического и гармонического, получившего имя от самой гармонии.
quotes.en: It is proper to harmony to construct and frame those systems according to some one of these genera of melody (you might roughly call it the measured shaping of song, or of a tune), which are the diatonic, the chromatic, and the harmonic, to which the name has fallen from Harmony itself.

readings.construal: Melodic movement or shaping of singing or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить и стройно сочетать эти системы сообразно одному из родов мелодии (её можно приблизительно определить как мелодическое движение пения или напева). Это диатонический, хроматический и гармонический роды. Последний получил имя от самой гармонии.
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct and arrange these systems according to one of the genera of melody (which one might broadly call the melodic movement of singing or of a tune). These are the diatonic, chromatic, and harmonic genera. The last takes its name from harmony itself.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить эти системы и согласовывать их с одним из следующих родов мелодии (мелодией, пожалуй, можно назвать мелодический строй пения или напева). Эти роды — диатонический, хроматический и гармонический, получивший имя от самой гармонии.
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct these systems and fit them to one of the following genera of melody (one might perhaps describe melody as the melodic shaping of singing or of a tune). The genera are the diatonic, the chromatic and the harmonic, which takes its name from harmony itself.

readings.construal: In Russian melodic movement. In English uses ‘modulation’, intending a classical sense explained in the note.

quotes.ru: Свойство гармонии — строить и слаживать эти системы применительно к какому-либо из этих родов мелодии (её, пожалуй, можно было бы назвать мелодическим движением пения или напева), каковы диатонический, хроматический и гармонический, которому имя досталось от самой Гармонии.
quotes.en: It is proper to harmony to construct and attune those systems for some one of these genera of melody (you might almost call it the modulation of song or tune), which are the diatonic, the chromatic and the harmonic, to which [last] the name fell from Harmony itself.

divergences.verdict: The lexical sense is regulated or measured succession in singing or in a tune. A/B/D are usable descriptions. Modern English ‘modulation’ ordinarily implies a change of key, which is foreign to the definition of melodia.
divergences.recommended_ru: её можно было бы назвать размеренным движением пения или напева
divergences.recommended_en: one might describe it as the measured shaping of singing or of a tune
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. modulor, use of singing and measured voice, Scaife ATLAS [checked]
Lewis & Short, s.v. modulatio, rhythmical measure and singing, Corpus of Latin Dictionaries [checked]
Boethius, De institutione musica, ed. Friedlein (1867), I.21 [checked]

errors.quote: the modulation of song or tune
errors.problem: In modern musical prose ‘modulation’ implies a key change unless explicitly qualified. The note explains the different sense, but the running term should already convey it.
errors.fix: Use ‘measured movement’ or ‘melodic shaping’ in the running text.

best_ru.why: Clear syntax and an intelligible parenthetical definition of melodia.

best_en.why: Both preserve the three genera, the application to systems and the parenthetical gloss without suggesting a key change.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep Xylander’s alternation between diatonon here and diatonicum elsewhere. The project's harmonic denotes the genus conventionally called enharmonic, and Xylander explicitly connects its name with harmony.

astra.sense: Harmony characteristically constructs these systems and fits them together according to one of the genera of melody. Melody might approximately be called the modulation of song or tune. The genera are diatonic, chromatic and harmonic. The last takes its name from harmony itself.

divergences.issue: What defines melody in the parenthesis?

readings.construal: A measured shaping of song or tune.

readings.construal: The melodic movement of singing or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить и стройно сочетать эти системы сообразно одному из родов мелодии (её можно приблизительно определить как мелодическое движение пения или напева).
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct and arrange these systems according to one of the genera of melody (which one might broadly call the melodic movement of singing or of a tune).

readings.construal: Russian has melodic movement, English ‘modulation’, in a historical sense explained in a note.

quotes.ru: Свойство гармонии — строить и слаживать эти системы применительно к какому-либо из этих родов мелодии (её, пожалуй, можно было бы назвать мелодическим движением пения или напева), каковы диатонический, хроматический и гармонический, которому имя досталось от самой Гармонии.

readings.construal: The melodic shaping or structure of singing or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить эти системы и согласовывать их с одним из следующих родов мелодии (мелодией, пожалуй, можно назвать мелодический строй пения или напева).
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct these systems and fit them to one of the following genera of melody (one might perhaps describe melody as the melodic shaping of singing or of a tune).

divergences.verdict: All take cantus and cantilenae with modulationem. The pertinent sense is measured or melodic shaping of sound. Unqualified modern ‘modulation’ can evoke change of key, but C explains the older meaning. Preserve the two genitives and the provisional fere.
divergences.recommended_ru: мелодический строй пения или напева
divergences.recommended_en: the melodic shaping of singing or of a tune

errors.quote: мерным ведением пения, или напева
errors.problem: Ведение пения can suggest directing the act of singing. The gloss is about the measured musical shaping of the sound.
errors.fix: «мерным движением пения или напева»

text_issues_review.printed: eam cantus seu cantilenae modulationem fere dixeris
text_issues_review.proposal: ‘modulation’ or ‘melodic ordering’
text_issues_review.why: Melodic ordering and measured shaping are both defensible. Modulation is historically possible if its modern tonal meaning is excluded.
evidence: Xylander, Basel (1556), 47.21–48.1 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]

best_ru.why: Separates the three genera from the parenthetic gloss and identifies the final antecedent.

best_en.why: ‘Melodic shaping’ distinguishes the explanatory term from melody while avoiding the modern sense of a key change.

notes_to_keep.gist: Xylander uses diatonon in the list but diatonicum later. The genus named harmonicum corresponds to Boethius’ enharmonic, and the derivation from harmonia needs to remain audible.

editor_questions: Agree an English rendering for modulatio that will also work elsewhere in Xylander.

X45.latin: Nam siquidem harmonia ipsa seu consonantiarum coaptatio potissimum per tonos progrediatur, eo modo diatonicum conficitur genus melodiae: sin per semitonia, chromaticum, quasi coloratum dicas: sin ipsa harmonia diesibus maiore sui parte absolvatur, harmonicus eo modo cantus conflatur.

claude.sense: For if harmony itself, or the fitting together (coaptatio) of consonances, proceeds chiefly by tones, the diatonic genus of melody is produced in that way; if by semitones, the chromatic, as if you said 'coloured'; but if harmony itself is completed for the greater part by dieses, harmonic song (cantus) is formed in that way.

errors.quote: Если сама гармония … / If harmony itself …
errors.problem: 'Nam', which makes this sentence the explanation of the three genera just named in X44, is left out (D also drops 'ipsa' in the last clause).
errors.fix: Ибо если сама гармония … / For if harmony itself …

best_ru.why: Both complete; keep 'Nam', 'ipsa', 'eo modo' and the gloss on chromaticum.

best_en.why: Both exact.

notes_to_keep.gist: coaptatio is the word Augustine coined for ἁρμονία (L&S s.v. coaptatio); quasi coloratum = etymological gloss on chromaticum, cf. Boethius I.21 'Chroma autem, quod dicitur color'.
'Chiefly' = two of the three steps of the tetrachord are of the named kind in each genus (T T S; S S trihemitone; D D ditone), as the following examples show.

sol.sense: Predominantly tonal motion produces the diatonic genus. Motion by semitones produces the chromatic, literally as if coloured. Harmony realized for the most part by dieses produces harmonic singing.

errors.quote: Diatonon and chromaticum are the names of the diatonic and chromatic genera.
errors.problem: The statement correctly describes X44, but in this passage the adduced Latin form is diatonicum, not diatonon.
errors.fix: Identify the X44 form as a variant and give diatonicum for X45.

best_ru.why: Both provide natural descriptions and keep the colour gloss.

best_en.why: Clear conditional structure and accurate rendering of the three genera and of the gloss.

notes_to_keep.gist: Read predominance as the number of smaller steps of the characteristic type in each tetrachord. This explains the two dieses of X51 despite the greater total width of the ditone.

astra.sense: If harmony, the fitting together of consonances, moves chiefly by tones, the diatonic genus of melody results. If by semitones, the chromatic, as if one said coloured. If harmony is for the most part realized by dieses, a harmonic song is formed.

errors.quote: гармония большей своей частью выполняется диесами
errors.problem: Выполняться диесами is an opaque calque for the composition of harmony from dieses.
errors.fix: гармония по большей части складывается из диес

best_ru.why: Makes the fitting of consonances intelligible, then distinguishes the three ways in which harmony proceeds.

best_en.why: The three parallel conditionals and the coloured gloss are clear.

notes_to_keep.gist: In the fourths that follow, two of the three steps are of the characteristic size. This explains ‘chiefly’ by number of steps rather than by the span they occupy.
For the colour explanation of chromaticum compare Boethius, De musica I.21, TML, Migne text [checked].

X46.latin: Neque tamen aut solis ex tonis universa harmonia componitur, aut ex solis semitoniis, solisve diesibus: id enim fieri nequit.

claude.sense: Yet the whole harmony is not composed of tones alone, or of semitones alone, or of dieses alone: for that cannot be.

errors.quote: При этом гармония в целом не складывается …
errors.problem: 'При этом' ('at the same time') does not render the adversative 'Neque tamen' ('yet … not'); the English has 'Yet'.
errors.fix: Однако гармония в целом не складывается …

best_ru.why: Exact, with 'tamen' and 'enim' rendered; B equally good but drops 'enim'.

best_en.why: Exact; B's 'cannot be composed' modalises the indicative 'componitur'.

sol.sense: Harmony as a whole cannot consist exclusively of tones, exclusively of semitones, or exclusively of dieses.

best_ru.why: Both preserve the three independent exclusions in natural Russian.

best_en.why: Keeps the assertion followed by the grounds in a second sentence.

astra.sense: Harmony in its entirety cannot be composed exclusively of tones, of semitones, or of dieses.

best_ru.why: The three matched negatives make the exclusions clear.

best_en.why: Accurately distributes ‘alone’ over each of the three interval classes.

X47.latin: Sed quoniam quidem tribus ex intervallis constat diatessaron, comprehensum videlicet duobus tonis et semitonio: in harmoniam coaptatis duobus tonis, opus est reliquum semitonio perfici.

claude.sense: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, being comprised, namely, by two tones and a semitone: when two tones have been fitted into the harmony, the remainder must be completed by a semitone; (continued in X48)

errors.quote: Кварта ведь состоит … / Since the fourth consists …
errors.problem: 'Sed', which opposes this to X46 ('not of tones alone … but since …'), is left out.
errors.fix: Но так как кварта состоит … / But since the fourth consists …

best_ru.why: Both exact; A also keeps the run-on into X48 with its semicolon, as the lower-case 'hocque' requires.

best_en.why: Both exact.

notes_to_keep.gist: Here the fourth is exactly two tones and a semitone, without the 'small remainder' of X34 (A, B, D note the same); comprehensum (neuter) agrees with diatessaron.
With 4:3 and 9:8 the actual remainder is 256/243.

sol.sense: The fourth here has three steps, named as two tones and a semitone. With the two tones fitted into the harmony, the remaining part must be completed with a semitone.

best_ru.why: Gives the three steps and brackets its supplied noun.

best_en.why: Clear syntax and accurate step count.

notes_to_keep.gist: With a Pythagorean fourth and the 9:8 tone, the remainder after two tones is 256:243. Point out that X47 itself has no further increment of the kind named at X34.

astra.sense: The fourth consists of three intervals, namely two tones and a semitone. Once two tones have been fitted into a harmony, the remainder must be completed by a semitone.

divergences.latin: comprehensum videlicet duobus tonis et semitonio
divergences.issue: Does the phrase describe the fourth as comprised by or as encompassing the steps?

readings.construal: The fourth is comprised or bounded by the steps.

quotes.ru: Но поскольку кварта состоит из трёх интервалов, а именно охватывается двумя тонами и полутоном, то, когда в гармонию прилажены два тона, остальное необходимо довершить полутоном;
quotes.en: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, being comprised, namely, by two tones and a semitone:

quotes.ru: Но так как кварта состоит из трёх интервалов, а именно заключена в двух тонах и полутоне, то, когда в гармонию прилажены два тона, остаток должен быть восполнен полутоном.
quotes.en: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, being comprised, namely, by two tones and a semitone, when two tones have been fitted into the harmony, the remainder must be completed by a semitone.

readings.construal: Restates the constituents in apposition.

quotes.ru: Но поскольку кварта состоит из трёх интервалов, а именно из двух тонов и полутона, после соединения двух тонов в гармонию остающееся [место] необходимо заполнить полутоном.
quotes.en: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, namely two tones and a semitone, the remainder must be filled with a semitone once two tones have been fitted into the harmony.

readings.construal: The fourth encompasses or spans them.

quotes.ru: Кварта ведь состоит из трёх интервалов и охватывает два тона и полутон.
quotes.en: Since the fourth consists of three intervals, spanning two tones and a semitone, once the two tones have been fitted together in harmony the remainder must be made up with a semitone.

divergences.verdict: The Latin participle is passive, agreeing with diatessaron. The two tones and semitone delimit the span of the fourth. B gives its musical content naturally, although an explicit ‘spanned by’ preserves the direction of the participle.
divergences.recommended_ru: кварта охватывается двумя тонами и полутоном
divergences.recommended_en: the fourth is spanned by two tones and a semitone
evidence: Lewis and Short, s.v. comprehendo [from memory]
Xylander, Basel (1556), 48.10–14 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]

best_ru.why: Gives the three intervals and the act of completing the fourth clearly.

best_en.why: The English reads continuously from the three constituent intervals to the remaining semitone.

notes_to_keep.gist: At X34 a further quantity was added. Here the two tones leave simply a semitone.

X48.latin: hocque genus diatessaron, diatonicum vocatur: quanquam ad eius constitutionem, praeter duos tonos, semitonium quoque accesserit.

claude.sense: (continuing X47) and this genus of the fourth is called diatonic, although a semitone too has entered into its constitution besides the two tones.

best_ru.why: Both exact, keep 'hocque' as the continuation of X47 and the perfect 'accesserit'; D equally clear.

best_en.why: Both exact; D's present 'enters' is an acceptable idiom.

notes_to_keep.gist: The concession is explained by the name ('proceeding through tones'): Boethius I.21 'vocatur diatonum, quasi quod per tonum ac per tonum progrediatur' (A makes the same point by cross-reference to X45–46).

sol.sense: This arrangement of the fourth is called diatonic even though a semitone enters the structure in addition to the two tones.

best_ru.why: Natural and exact.

best_en.why: Keeps the concession and makes clear which notes enter the genus.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain the concession by the etymological association of diatonic with proceeding through tones, with Boethius I.21 as a parallel.

astra.sense: This genus of the fourth is called diatonic, even though a semitone as well as two tones has entered its construction.

errors.quote: The semitone is the third.
errors.problem: This is the third item by the order of exposition. The text does not specify its position in a performance running from low to high. Vitruvius V.4.3, 6, distinguishes the steps by their bounding notes [checked].
errors.fix: Say that one of the three steps is a semitone, or specify the order being counted.

best_ru.why: «В его состав … входит» expresses constitution naturally.

best_en.why: The concessive clause identifies the semitone as a constituent despite the genus name.

notes_to_keep.gist: Boethius explains diatonic by progression through tones. The concession here acknowledges the additional semitone. Boethius, De musica I.21, TML, Migne text [checked].

X49.latin: Iam si duo sint semitonia, quod superest, ex coalitu utique conflatur intervallum, trisemitonium incompositum:

claude.sense: Now if there are two semitones, what remains is assuredly formed by coalescence into one interval, the incomposite trihemitone; (continued in X50)

errors.quote: то из остатка путём слияния образуется интервал / the remainder coalesces into an interval
errors.problem: 'utique' ('assuredly, necessarily'), which marks the result as forced by the size of the fourth, is left out.
errors.fix: то остаток непременно путём слияния образует интервал / the remainder necessarily coalesces into an interval

best_ru.why: Complete (Iam, utique, ex coalitu) and exact.

best_en.why: Same.

notes_to_keep.gist: coalitus is a late word (Arnobius, L&S); its sense here answers to 'coalescentibus' in X27: three semitones fused into one incomposite interval (C says the same).
Why 'incomposite trihemitone': three semitones in size, taken as one step in melody.

sol.sense: When two of the intervals are semitones, the remaining span forms one incomposite trihemitone by coalescence.

errors.quote: fused by coalescence / сплавляется, через слияние
errors.problem: The literal verbal doubling is ungainly, especially the Russian inserted commas. It can be preserved better by choosing complementary words.
errors.fix: Use ‘is formed by coalescence’ / «образуется путём слияния».

best_ru.why: Clear sequence and idiomatic word order.

best_en.why: Keeps utique and describes the single resulting interval precisely.

notes_to_keep.gist: A span equivalent to three semitones sounds as one step, so it is incomposite in this context. Boethius I.23 explains the same distinction.

astra.sense: With two semitones, the interval remaining is formed by coalescence: an incomposite trihemitone.

divergences.issue: Is the author's affirmation audible?

readings.construal: Translate the assurance.

quotes.ru: Если же полутонов будет два, то остаток непременно сплавляется, через слияние, в [один] интервал — несоставной трёхполутон;
quotes.en: Now if there be two semitones, what is left over is assuredly fused by coalescence into an interval, the incomposite trihemitone;

quotes.ru: Если же полутонов два, то оставшееся, разумеется, путём срастания слагается в интервал — несоставной трёхполутон;

divergences.verdict: Paean and hymenaeus are established names that a reader of classics understands, so keeping them (A, B, C) is right; D's 'wedding song' is also correct. Exodius is the real problem: Xylander only Latinizes the Greek word and gives no hint of its sense, which may be the closing song (ἐξόδιον, Pollux) or, in Byzantine usage, a funeral hymn (D's doubt). The transliteration (A, C) keeps Xylander's indeterminacy but Russian «эксодий» also names the Roman afterpiece (exodium); B's 'exit song' and D's 'song of departure' choose a sense. Recommend the name with a note giving both possible senses; editor's choice.

errors.fix: Но, кроме того, каждый из них видоизменяется … Ибо слаживается то лидийский … / But each of these is moreover varied … For now a Lydian …

text_issues_review.printed: Pæan, Hymenæus, Exodius (49.17)
text_issues_review.proposal: погребальная песнь / funeral song
text_issues_review.why: In Byzantine Greek ἐξόδιος (ὕμνος) is used of funeral song (D cites the Holy Saturday canon), which suits a Greek text of 1008; but whether Xylander meant it is unknowable from his Latin. Best kept in a note, not in the running text.
evidence: Canon of Holy Saturday, ode 1, first troparion ('ἐξόδιον ὕμνον καὶ ἐπιτάφιον ᾠδήν'), agreeing with D's citation [from memory]

best_ru.why: Complete (Verum, praeterea, enim, quaecunque), the plural 'melodiarum' kept, the genre names consistent with the Latin.

best_en.why: Same.

notes_to_keep.gist: Exodius: song of departure (Pollux IV.108, exit song of the chorus); in the Byzantine Holy Saturday canon the cognate epithet marks a burial hymn (to be verified).

Latin exodium = afterpiece following a tragedy, Greek ἐξόδιον = closing song of a tragedy; Xylander's masculine Exodius agrees with Paean and Hymenaeus; 'Vide Annot.' in the margin at 49.17 (also D, B).
unamquamque and melodiarum are corrections of the printed text (unamquan- with -que sign; meliodiarum).

editor_questions: Exodius: keep the name (эксодий / exodius) with a note on its two possible senses, or describe ('exit song' B, 'song of departure' D)?

sol.sense: Each genus admits subdivisions and varieties of singing. Tunes can be Lydian, Phrygian or Dorian. Each type of tune can accommodate a paean, hymenaeus, exodius or other kind of melody.

divergences.latin: ad quarum unamquamque Paean, Hymenaeus, Exodius
divergences.issue: Should Exodius be transliterated, glossed as an exit or closing song, or narrowed to a funerary occasion?

readings.construal: Retains the Latinizing genre name in the running text and offers theatrical or exit etymology in the note.

quotes.ru: Но каждый из них сверх того видоизменяется и расходится на немалое число разделений, различий и видов пения. Ибо слаживается то лидийский, то фригийский, а там и дорийский напев; и к каждому из них приспосабливаются пеан, гименей, эксодий и какие ни есть другие роды мелодий.
quotes.en: But each of these is moreover varied, and is drawn out into not a few divisions, differences and species of songs. For now a Lydian, now a Phrygian, presently also a Dorian tune is framed; and to each of these the paean, the hymenaeus, the exodius and whatever other kinds of melodies there are, are adapted.

quotes.ru: Но, кроме того, каждый из них видоизменяется и распадается на немалое число разделений, различий и видов пения. Ибо слаживается то лидийский, то фригийский, а затем и дорийский напев; и к каждому из них приспосабливаются пеан, гименей, эксодий и любые другие роды мелодий.
quotes.en: Moreover, each of these is varied and split into not a few divisions, differences and species of song. For now a Lydian, now a Phrygian, and then also a Dorian tune is attuned; and to each of them the paean, the hymenaeus, the exodius and whatever other genera of melodies are adapted.

readings.construal: An exit song or closing song.

quotes.ru: Далее, каждый из них меняется и распадается на немало подразделений, разновидностей и видов пения. Ведь складывается то лидийский напев, то фригийский, а затем и дорийский. К каждому из них прилаживают пеан, гименей, заключительную песнь и иные роды мелодии.
quotes.en: Each of these, moreover, is varied and subdivided into quite a few divisions, varieties, and kinds of singing. Now a Lydian tune is arranged, now a Phrygian, and then a Dorian as well. To each of these are fitted the paean, the hymenaeus, the exit song, and any other genera of melody.

readings.construal: A song of departure, with a more specifically funerary alternative considered in the doubts.

quotes.ru: Каждый из этих [родов], в свою очередь, допускает изменения и распадается на немалое число подразделений, разновидностей и видов пения. Складывается то лидийский, то фригийский, то дорийский напев. К каждому из них приспосабливают пеан, свадебную песнь, прощальную песнь и любые другие роды мелодий.
quotes.en: Each of these [genera] in turn admits of variation and divides into no small number of divisions, varieties and species of singing. A tune is fashioned now as Lydian, now as Phrygian, then again as Dorian. To each of these the paean, the wedding song, the song of departure and any other genera of melodies are fitted.

divergences.verdict: The list stands without definitions in Xylander. A broad ‘exit song’ discloses the lexical sense without supplying an occasion. ‘Song of departure’ is also possible, while Russian «прощальная песнь» leans towards the act of saying farewell. A funeral is not implied by the local list and has to remain a separate hypothesis.
divergences.recommended_ru: пеан, свадебная песнь и заключительная песнь
divergences.recommended_en: the paean, wedding song and exit song
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. exodium; LSJ, s.v. ἐξόδιος [from memory]

text_issues_review.printed: Pæan, Hymenæus, Exodius
text_issues_review.proposal: погребальная песнь / funeral song
text_issues_review.why: The text does not identify the song's occasion. The cited liturgical witness and the proposed application to Xylander's Exodius are not verified. A funerary use of a cognate would establish a possible parallel, but does not by itself determine this genre's meaning.
evidence: Holy Saturday canon, ode I, first troparion [from memory]

best_ru.why: Retains the tune terminology and conveys the third song's basic closing or exit sense without assuming a funeral.

best_en.why: Clear distinction between classes of tunes and kinds of song.

notes_to_keep.gist: Preserve the difference from Vinet’s modulus. Xylander groups Lydian, Phrygian and Dorian as varieties of tune. The song genres can be matched to any of them.
The printed margin beside the song names points to the annotations. Keep the cross-reference and explain the song names independently.

editor_questions: If retaining the Latin-style song names, give their genre meanings at first occurrence. The sense of Exodius can be left general.

astra.sense: Each genus is further varied and divided into numerous divisions, distinctions and species of song. A Lydian, Phrygian or Dorian tune is fashioned in turn, and a paean, wedding song, exodius and other kinds of melody can be fitted to each.

divergences.issue: Named genre, exit song, or song of farewell?

readings.construal: Retain the historical name.

quotes.ru: и к каждому из них приспосабливаются пеан, гименей, эксодий и какие ни есть другие роды мелодий.
quotes.en: and to each of these the paean, the hymenaeus, the exodius and whatever other kinds of melodies there are, are adapted.

quotes.en: and to each of them the paean, the hymenaeus, the exodius and whatever other genera of melodies are adapted.

readings.construal: Describes the closing or exit song.

quotes.ru: К каждому из них прилаживают пеан, гименей, заключительную песнь и иные роды мелодии.
quotes.en: To each of these are fitted the paean, the hymenaeus, the exit song, and any other genera of melody.

readings.construal: Russian calls it a farewell, English a song of departure.

quotes.ru: К каждому из них приспосабливают пеан, свадебную песнь, прощальную песнь и любые другие роды мелодий.
quotes.en: To each of these the paean, the wedding song, the song of departure and any other genera of melodies are fitted.

divergences.verdict: The transmitted masculine functions as a genre name in a list with Paean and Hymenaeus. An exit or closing song is a useful gloss. Farewell or burial would add an occasion the Latin does not give. Pollux records a choral song sung on departure, a specific parallel for the broad exit gloss.
divergences.recommended_ru: эксодий [заключительная песнь]
divergences.recommended_en: an exodius [exit song]
evidence: Xylander, Basel (1556), 49.12–18 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]
Pollux, Onomasticon IV.108, ed. I. Bekker (1846), p. 168 [checked]

errors.quote: прощальную песнь
errors.problem: The noun makes saying farewell the song’s subject or occasion. Exodius can name a song accompanying an exit or closing an action. The Latin leaves its occasion open.
errors.fix: «эксодий» with a note ‘песнь при выходе или в завершение действия’.

text_issues_review.printed: Exodius
text_issues_review.proposal: погребальная песнь / funeral song
text_issues_review.why: Pollux attests a song at the exit of a chorus. The Latin list gives no occasion that requires a funeral. The separate liturgical reference advanced for the funerary possibility was not verified.
evidence: Xylander, Basel (1556), 49.12–18 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]
Pollux, Onomasticon IV.108, ed. I. Bekker (1846), p. 168 [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: cantuum diuisiones, differentias atque species
text_issues_review.proposal: divisions, differences and species of songs
text_issues_review.why: The one genitive precedes a coordinated series of three accusatives. The content of all three is supplied by the singing or songs under discussion.
evidence: Allen and Greenough, Genitive with Nouns [from memory]

best_ru.why: The three forms of singing are intelligible, with the last left broad.

best_en.why: Exit song avoids restricting exodius to a specific dramatic or funerary occasion.

notes_to_keep.gist: Lydian, Phrygian and Dorian qualify cantilena. The three song forms that follow can each fit any of these tunes. The print points to annotations in the margin.

editor_questions: Keep the masculine genre name exodius with a gloss, or use a descriptive exit/closing song?
Does Exodius merit a historical genre label with a gloss for its possible occasions?

X57.latin: Neque enim sola intervallorum mutatione, aut eorum discrimine, sed praeterea etiam obliquioribus aut celerioribus transitibus, mansionibus, fluxibus, tum tactuum ipsorum pulsationumque variis administrationibus, innumera, atque plane varia cantilenarum genera comparantur.

claude.sense: For not by the change of intervals alone, or by their distinction, but besides also by more oblique or swifter transitions, by stays (on a note), by flowings, and then by the various handlings of the touches and strokes themselves, innumerable and quite varied kinds of cantilenae are produced.

errors.quote: Innumerable and quite varied kinds of tune are obtained by changing or varying the intervals, and also by more oblique or swifter transitions
errors.problem: 'Neque enim sola … sed praeterea etiam' loses 'not … alone' and 'for'; 'eorum discrimine' (their distinction) becomes 'varying'. The Russian keeps 'не только … но также'.
errors.fix: For innumerable and quite varied kinds of tune are obtained not only by the change of intervals or their distinction, but also by …

errors.quote: как от смены интервалов и различий между ними, так и от … / both from changes of interval … and from …
errors.problem: 'not by … alone, but also' is flattened into 'both … and', losing 'sola'; in the Russian 'variis administrationibus' becomes 'от того, как исполняются', dropping 'variis'.
errors.fix: не только сменой интервалов или их различием, но кроме того … и разнообразным обращением с самими касаниями и ударами / not by the change of intervals alone … but also … and by the various handlings of the touches and strokes

errors.quote: by dwellings, by flowings
errors.problem: 'dwellings' for mansionibus reads as 'houses' in English; the musical sense is stays or rests on a note (the Russian 'остановками' is right).
errors.fix: by stays, by flowings

text_issues_review.printed: tum tactuum ipso-|rum pulsationumqúe uarijs administrationibus (49.21–22)
text_issues_review.proposal: разнообразным управлением самими тактами и ударами / by the varied handling of the very beats and strokes
text_issues_review.why: A's choice 'touches' is supported by classical usage of tactus of strings beside pulsatio; but tactus is also the standard sixteenth-century term for the musical beat, and the context (swifter transitions, stays, flowings) is partly temporal, so a Renaissance reader may have heard 'beats'. Both are possible for Xylander's Latin.
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. tactus I: 'quae (chordae) ad quemque tactum respondeant', Cic. de Or. 3.57.216 [checked]
tactus as the measure-beat in sixteenth-century theory (e.g. Gaffurius, Practica musicae) [from memory]

best_ru.why: Both complete ('не одной лишь … но сверх того и …', 'разнообразным управлением / обращением с самими касаниями и ударами').

best_en.why: Complete and exact, with 'stays' for mansionibus; A equally exact but 'dwellings' misleads.

notes_to_keep.gist: A list of means of melodic composition (transitus, mansiones, fluxus, tactus, pulsationes); compare the parts of melopoeia in Cleonides; tactus also 'beat' in the sixteenth century, here rather 'touch'.

obliquioribus 'more slanting, roundabout' against celerioribus; Vinet has lentioribus 'slower' here — the versions differ (D notes the same); mansio cf. Aristoxenus' μονή τις καὶ στάσις τῆς φωνῆς (LSJ s.v. μονή).

editor_questions: tactus: 'touch' (of strings) or the Renaissance 'beat'? A note giving both seems advisable.

sol.sense: Variety in tunes arises through differences and changes in intervals, less direct or faster transitions, lingerings and flowing passages, and the various ways touches and strokes are executed.

divergences.issue: Are these both acts of varying intervals, or a change and an inherent distinction?

readings.construal: A change of intervals and a difference or distinction between them; B Russian likewise distinguishes the two.

quotes.ru: Ибо не одной лишь переменой интервалов или их различием, но сверх того и более окольными или более быстрыми переходами, остановками, течениями, а также разнообразным управлением самими касаниями и ударами создаются бесчисленные и совершенно разнообразные роды напевов.
quotes.en: For not by the change of intervals alone, or by their distinction, but in addition also by more oblique or swifter transitions, by dwellings, by flowings, and further by the varied handling of the very touches and strokes, innumerable and altogether various kinds of tunes are brought about.

quotes.ru: Ведь не только изменением интервалов или их различием, но, кроме того, ещё и более окольными или более быстрыми переходами, задержками, течениями, а также разнообразным обращением с самими касаниями и ударами достигаются бесчисленные и вполне разнообразные роды напевов.
quotes.en: For not only by the change of intervals or their distinction, but besides also by more oblique or swifter transitions, by stays, by flowings, and by various handlings of the touches themselves and of the strokes, innumerable and altogether varied genera of tunes are obtained.

quotes.ru: Ведь бесчисленные и поистине разнообразные виды напевов возникают как от смены интервалов и различий между ними, так и от более извилистых или более быстрых переходов, остановок и непрерывного движения, а также от того, как исполняются сами прикосновения и удары.
quotes.en: For the countless and indeed varied kinds of tune result both from changes of interval or differences between intervals and from more winding or swifter transitions, from points of rest and passages of flowing movement, and from the various ways the touches and strokes themselves are executed.

readings.construal: English treats both as acts, ‘by changing or varying the intervals’.

quotes.ru: Бесчисленные и весьма разнообразные роды напева получаются не только от перемены интервалов или различий между ними, но также от более непрямых или более быстрых переходов, задержек, плавных движений и от разных способов касания и удара.
quotes.en: Innumerable and quite varied kinds of tune are obtained by changing or varying the intervals, and also by more oblique or swifter transitions, lingering and flowing movements, and different ways of managing the touches and strokes themselves.

divergences.verdict: Mutatione denotes changing them, while discrimine denotes difference, distinction or separation. The coordination is meaningful and preserved by B Russian and the other translations. B English does not let the reader distinguish the second source of variety.
divergences.recommended_ru: от перемены интервалов или различий между ними
divergences.recommended_en: through changes in the intervals or differences between them
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.vv. mutatio and discrimen [from memory]
Lewis & Short, s.v. discrimen II.A, difference and musical differentiation, Logeion [checked]

divergences.issue: Are mansiones pauses, sustained positions or lingerings, and are fluxus necessarily uninterrupted?

readings.construal: Literally ‘dwellings’ and ‘flowings’; Russian sounds like stops and flows.
