quotes.ru: Ведь бесчисленные и поистине разнообразные виды напевов возникают как от смены интервалов и различий между ними, так и от более извилистых или более быстрых переходов, остановок и непрерывного движения, а также от того, как исполняются сами прикосновения и удары.
quotes.en: For the countless and indeed varied kinds of tune result both from changes of interval or differences between intervals and from more winding or swifter transitions, from points of rest and passages of flowing movement, and from the various ways the touches and strokes themselves are executed.

divergences.verdict: Read the two as complements within melodic movement: dwelling, possibly on a sustained note, versus flowing motion. A complete stop and strict uninterruptedness are more specific than the words. Vinet’s different noun for pauses can be kept distinct.
divergences.recommended_ru: задержками и плавным движением
divergences.recommended_en: through lingering and flowing movement
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.vv. mansio and fluxus [from memory]

errors.quote: by changing or varying the intervals
errors.problem: Both gerunds describe changing intervals and merge the distinct discrimen.
errors.fix: Use ‘through changes in the intervals or differences between them’.

errors.quote: by dwellings, by flowings
errors.problem: ‘Dwellings’ can mean buildings and the pair is plainly unidiomatic in this setting.
errors.fix: Use ‘through lingering and flowing movement’.

errors.quote: непрерывного движения
errors.problem: Fluxus means flowing movement without an explicit statement that it is uninterrupted.
errors.fix: Use «плавного движения» or «течения» with a note.

text_issues_review.printed: tactuum ipsorum pulsationumqúe uarijs administrationibus
text_issues_review.proposal: разнообразным управлением самими тактами и ударами / by the varied handling of the very beats and strokes
text_issues_review.why: Renaissance tactus can denote a beat, but pulsationes and the parallel descriptions of performance make execution of touches and strokes plausible. ‘Beat’ here would commit the text to a rhythmic interpretation not decisively established.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. tactus; DMLBS, s.v. pulsatio [from memory]

best_ru.why: Keeps the opposition between changing intervals and differences between them, and avoids a purely rhythmic reading of tactus.

best_en.why: Preserves the categories and the distinction from Vinet with clear prose. Render mansiones as lingering to avoid silence.

notes_to_keep.gist: Do not equate Xylander’s obliquioribus, ‘less direct’, with Vinet’s adjective of slowness. The Latin does not name a particular technique.
Mansio denotes staying or lingering and can be explained as dwelling on a sound. The instrumental or rhythmic application of tactus is worth noting only if supported.

editor_questions: How narrowly should the last terms be glossed as instrumental execution? Keep the neutral ‘touches and strokes’ until the playing technique is established.

quotes.ru: Бесчисленные и весьма разнообразные роды напева получаются не только от перемены интервалов или различий между ними, но также от более непрямых или более быстрых переходов, задержек, плавных движений и от разных способов касания и удара.

divergences.verdict: All construe the word alike (Vitruvian ‘commensurability of the parts of a whole’). Lewis & Short gloss symmetria ‘proportion, symmetry’ and Gaffiot ‘symétrie’, so B's and D's ‘symmetry’ is dictionary-supported and not an error. But modern English ‘symmetry’ suggests mirror symmetry and may mislead a modern reader (about.md § 4.1), and the dictionary's other gloss, ‘proportion’, is already taken by proportio. ‘Commensurability’ renders συμμετρία in its first LSJ sense and matches the Russian «соразмерность»; ‘due measure’ (A) is acceptable but paraphrastic. text_issues_review.printed: ipsaque adeo Vniuersitas
text_issues_review.proposal: …и такова же сама Вселенная, поскольку музыка является гармонией и согласием Вселенной / …and so indeed is the Universe itself, since music is the harmony and accord of the universe.
text_issues_review.why: ipsaque adeo is the emphatic addition of a second predicate of Musica (‘and indeed the universe itself’); the following utpote quae clause explains exactly that identification. A itself rejects the alternative.
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. adeo II.B.1 (ipse adeo, for emphasis) and II.B.5 (atque adeo, adding a stronger point) [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: ipsaque adeo Vniuersitas
text_issues_review.proposal: и тем самым сама вселенная / and thus the universe itself
text_issues_review.why: Lewis & Short record a consequential ‘so, thus’ (adeo III.B), so B's alternative is lexically possible. But after a pronoun (ipsaque adeo) the emphatic use applies (II.B.1 ‘just, precisely’, ‘most freq. with pronouns’; cf. II.B.5 atque adeo ‘or even’), and ‘thus’ would turn the climax into an inference that the following utpote clause makes unnecessary. The difference in sense is slight; B itself keeps ‘indeed’.
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. adeo II.B.1, II.B.5, III.B [checked]

notes_to_keep.gist: Convenientia (Ciceronian ‘agreement, accord’) begins a chain of cognates: convenientia, conveniens in the definition of the note (V11), convenire (V15); render consistently (согласие – согласующийся – согласоваться / accord – accordant – accord).
Ipsaque adeo Universitas identifies music outright with the universe, not only with its harmony (cf. Xylander's harmonia universi).

editor_questions: Musica autem est ipsa per se symmetria et proportio, ipsaque adeo Universitas: all four take the first ipsa with Musica (‘music in itself is …’); the parallel ipsa … ipsaque would also allow ‘music is symmetria and proportion itself … and indeed the universe itself’. claude.sense: A note is the accordant (conveniens) tension or pitch (intensio) of a voice that has no interval.

divergences.verdict: Both are legitimate (about.md § 4.5 leaves intensio on its own to the translator). Lewis & Short record a musical sense (II ‘the tune’: gravis, media, acuta, Censor. 12), and the definition reflects the Greek τάσις (Thrasyllus in Theon: φθόγγος = φωνῆς ἐναρμονίου τάσις), usually rendered ‘pitch’. Vinet's other uses pull both ways: V37 in intensionibus remissionibusve (the raising/lowering pair fixed by § 4.5), V45 ab intensione acuti (pitch of the higher note), V47 torsione claviculorum … intensione and intensione spiritus ac remissione (physical tension, and the pair), V49 bis Dia-pason universam comprehendens intensionem (the whole compass). ‘Tension’ keeps the Latin image and the link with V47; ‘pitch’ is what a modern reader understands (§ 4.1). Whichever is chosen, the other belongs in a note, and the choice must be applied with V37, V45, V47 and V49 in view.

divergences.recommended_en: A note is the accordant pitch of a voice that has no interval (note: intensio, literally ‘tension’)

V16.latin: quoniam nisi sic elatus sit, absurdus et absonus sonus est, non conveniens: imo vero ne sonus quidem omnino vocandus, sed crepitus quidam temere editus, et ad convenientiam concentumque ineptus.

claude.sense: since, unless it has been so uttered, it is an out-of-tune and ill-sounding note, not an accordant one; nay rather it should not be called a note at all, but a kind of noise (crepitus) uttered at random, unfit for accord and concord.

best_ru.why: Both keep ‘not accordant’ as a contrast with the definition; C's «треск» renders crepitus most exactly.

best_en.why: Both exact; imo vero correctly as ‘or rather / indeed’.

notes_to_keep.gist: Absurdus et absonus is a Ciceronian pair (vox absona atque absurda, De or. 3.41); crepitus ‘rattling, clatter’, an unmusical sound; two words for one notion, as again convenientiam concentumque.
Xylander uses the more technical dissonus / consonus and strepitus here.

sol.sense: A sound not produced this way is harsh and discordant and lacks the required aptitude. It does not deserve the name note. It is noise produced at random and unfit for accord and concord.

best_ru.why: Both retain the paired objections and prefer general noise to more specific rattling or rumbling.

best_en.why: Both retain the note–noise distinction and the vocabulary of accord.

notes_to_keep.gist: Explain convenientia as an echo of the note's definition, with concentus as sounded concord (Vinet II.1, V11 and V15–V16 [checked]).

astra.sense: Unless so produced, the note is ill-sounding and out of tune, unfitting. Indeed it should by no means be called a note, but a kind of noise emitted at random, unfit for accord and concordant sounding.

best_ru.why: The two degrees of rejection and the distinction between noise and a note remain clear.

best_en.why: Out-of-tune, discordant and clatter preserve Vinet’s distinctions and his correction of the word note.

notes_to_keep.gist: Convenientia recalls the capacity for accord in the definition, while concentus concerns sounds sounding together.

Theon (Hiller p. 88.17–18, Thrasyllus' canon) calls the fourth note ὑπερυπάτη ἡ καὶ διάτονος ὑπατῶν; Vinet writes Paramese, Xylander paramesos.
Boethius names the fourth diatonic note lichanos hypaton diatonos (De inst. mus. I.20, I.22).

divergences.verdict: Both are grammatically possible. The logical sense is lexicalised (L&S conficio I.B.3, passive ‘to follow logically, be deduced’, with ex; Gaffiot: ex quo conficitur ut, Cic. Inv. 2.145; ex eo hoc conficitur … esse, Cic. Inv. 1.63), and humanist Latin often has quod for ut or for the accusative and infinitive. The composition reading has the stronger support inside this text: Vinet uses conficere for making up an interval from its parts (V39 Conficitur autem Dia-tessaron duobus tonis et hemitonio …; V55 ex tribus intervallis Dia-tessaron intervallum confectum est) and for melos and modulationes (V32, V65); ex his naturally means the fifteen notes just listed (cf. L&S I.A.1 unde pallium conficiatur, making from a material); and Xylander's parallel (Per has sonorum species heccaedecachordum … absolvitur) expresses composition. Prefer composition; C's reading is a defensible minority construal, not an error. The doctrine is the same either way, so the final choice is the editor's.

divergences.verdict: Grammatically open: eandem can resume chordam or semisesquioctavam (rationem); the neuter hemitonium is excluded. Xylander's parallel (et hoc denuo dividi in diesin, hoc = semitonium) shows that the doctrine is the halving of the semitone, which either reference yields. In English, ‘the same’ (A, C) keeps the ambiguity and is closest; B's bracket is a legitimate, marked decision. In Russian all four in effect choose the string, because «её» agrees only with «струну»; that is a legitimate reading, so the Russian renderings are not at fault, but A's doubt and C's note wrongly say that their Russian keeps the ambiguity (see errors). The other reference belongs in a note.

sol.sense: Arithmetic cannot split a given square number into equal square numbers in the example's intended halving, or double it to another square. Sixteen is 4². The resulting eight and thirty-two are neither square numbers nor realizable as square arrays of unit dots.

V29.latin: Quadrati enim latus Geometra si in diametrum traduxerit, et ei quadratum circumiecerit diametro, dimidium dati quadrati habebit, atque ex quadrati dimetiente rursus si latus Geometra effecerit, datum duplicaverit quadratum.

claude.sense: For if the geometer turns the side of a square into a diagonal and puts a square around that diagonal, he will have half the given square; and if in turn he makes a side out of the square's diagonal, he will have doubled the given square.

best_ru.why: Both follow circumiecerit (‘опишет около/вокруг’) and the future perfects closely.

best_en.why: Exact.

notes_to_keep.gist: Description of the geometric figure on p. 46: square ABDC, diagonals AD and BC meeting at E, F above BD; BFDE, with BD as diagonal, is half of ABDC; the doubled square is not drawn.
Read the other way, the same figure also shows the doubling: taking BFDE as given, ABDC stands on its diagonal and is twice its area.

The diagonal is named twice, diametrus (Greek) and dimetiens (its Latin calque, Pliny); the doubling of the square on its diagonal is the construction of Plato's Meno 82b–85b. Xylander has diameter in both places.

sol.sense: A square built with the old side as its diagonal has half the original area. A square built with the old diagonal as its side has twice the original area.

best_ru.why: Uses за and с to make each reciprocal construction unambiguous.

best_en.why: States the converse and both geometric operations plainly.

notes_to_keep.gist: Retain the description of p. 46, with ABCD's outside edges ordered A–B–D–C in the woodcut and diagonals AD and BC intersecting at E. Square BFDE uses BD as diagonal and has half the area. A doubled square from the original's diagonal is not drawn, though the given arrangement also illustrates doubling if BFDE is taken as the starting square (Tournon 1591, p. 46, supplied page image [checked]; Euclid, Elements I.47, ed. D. Lardner (1855), Trinity College Dublin [checked]).
Keep the lexical contrast between Vinet's diameter and substantival dimetiens and Xylander's repeated diameter (Vinet III.3 and supplied parallel in Xylander [checked]).

astra.sense: If the geometer makes the side of a square into a diagonal and constructs a square about that diagonal, he has half the given square. Conversely, making the diagonal of the square into a side doubles the given square.

V30.latin: Ad hunc sane modum et sesquioctava toni ratio in hemitonium dividitur, rursusque in diesin.

claude.sense: In just this way the sesquioctave [9:8] ratio of the tone too is divided into the semitone, and again into the diesis.

best_ru.why: Both render et (‘too’) and rursus, bracket present.

best_en.why: Exact.

notes_to_keep.gist: The analogy is exact: the side of the half-square is to the given side as 1 : √2, a mean proportional; half the tone 9:8 is the mean proportional √72 between 9 and 8, which no number expresses.
The argument defends the halving of the tone, against which Boethius argues in De inst. mus. III.1; Vinet's numbers in V22 (17:16, 33:32) are only approximations of the geometric half and quarter.

sol.sense: Vinet says the 9:8 ratio of a tone is divided in this same way to obtain a semitone, then a diesis.

best_ru.why: Clearly differentiates the first division and the repeated one.

best_en.why: Clearly states the result of each division without implying that both are cuts directly off the undivided tone.

notes_to_keep.gist: Give exact mathematical half and quarter ratios as conditional comparisons, √(9/8) and (9/8)^(1/4). Their comparison with 17:16 and 33:32 explains the distinction raised by the print’s geometrical analogy (Boethius, De institutione musica I.16 (Friedlein) and III.1 (Migne), 16:17:18 and unequal subintervals [checked]; Tournon 1591, p. 44, supplied page image and line AB [checked]; Tournon 1591, p. 45, supplied page image [checked]).

errors.fix: Give √72 as a length and √(9/8) as the interval ratio.

divergences.verdict: about.md § 4.2 fixes the term for compositum / incompositum (non compositum), not for simplex. Vinet uses simplicia here and in V32 (where he explains the name: Simplicia autem ideo dicta sunt …) and non-composita in V34; Xylander has incomposita. Keeping ‘simple’ keeps both Vinet's explanation of the name and the difference from non-composita and from Xylander visible, as the brief asks. V34.latin: sed haec non sine medio, neque non-composita sunt, quando per media omnia supradicta intervalla incedunt: quae ratione quidem vocis primi soni ad ultimum, intervalla appellantur: sed a numero tamen ordineque, qui in medio sunt, sonorum, haec nomina receperunt: Dia-tessaron, ut quod per quatuor: Dia-pente, per quinque: Dia-pason per octo sonos aut chordas ingrediatur termineturque.

claude.sense: But these [the fourth, fifth and octave] are not without a middle, nor are they incomposite, since they proceed through all the intervals named above as intermediate ones. They are called 'intervals' by reason of the voice of the first note [in relation] to the last, but they received these names from the number and order of the notes that lie in the middle: Dia-tessaron as that which proceeds through four, Dia-pente through five, Dia-pason through eight notes or strings, and is bounded by them.

divergences.verdict: The relation reading (A, C, D) keeps closer to the Latin as printed: Vinet has no a/ab before primi soni, and ratio ... ad is his normal construction for the relation of one note to another (V19 'quam ... rationem primus sonus ad octavum'; V22 'quomodo novem numerus ad octo'). B's span reading supplies a 'from' that the Latin lacks; it gives a defensible sense (Xylander's Latin, X29, has 'a primo sono ad extremum'), but that is the other version, not Vinet's wording. Russian «по отношению голоса первого звука к последнему» keeps both the word ratio and its 'respect' sense.

notes_to_keep.gist: Vinet introduces two classes without the etymological glosses found in Xylander. His next paragraph illustrates antiphony with octaves.
Boethius reports the Pythagorean objection to the octave plus fourth (8:3) and Ptolemy’s defense of its consonance (De institutione musica II.27 and V.9, ed. Friedlein [checked]).
Pseudo-Aristotle, Problemata XIX.39, 921a [checked], explicitly calls the octave antiphonic and illustrates it with different voices singing together.

Theon gives the same two class names and the four examples C specifies (ed. Hiller, p. 48.16–20 [checked]). Vinet also places the octave plus fourth and octave plus fifth in the antiphonic class. Gaudentius uses paraphonic for intervals between consonance and dissonance and gives the tritone and ditone as examples (Harmonic Introduction 8, ed. Jan, p. 338.3–7 [checked]).

claude.sense: The paraphonic and the antiphonic differ from each other in that the paraphonic is consonant in an unequal space of time, the notes taking one another up in a gentle, as it were, and fitting way, evenly, according to proportions and ratios; the antiphonic accords in an equal space of time, the high being consonant together with the low, as the eighth with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth: the low notes, that is, together with the high, or the high with the low, ascending or descending at the same time in an entirely equal proportion, in raisings or lowerings.

sol.sense: Paraphony is consonant in unequal time, with the notes smoothly and aptly taking one another up in regular proportion. Antiphony accords in equal time, with a high and low note sounding together. All four examples pair notes seven steps apart, and the paired high and low notes rise or fall together in equal proportion.

quotes.ru: Различаются же между собой парафония и антифония тем, что парафония консонирует в неравный промежуток времени, когда звуки неким образом мягко и уместно сменяют друг друга, равномерно, согласно пропорциям и отношениям; антифония же согласуется в равный промежуток времени, когда высокий [звук] консонирует вместе с низким, как восьмой с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым, — то есть когда низкие вместе с высокими или высокие с низкими в совершенно равной пропорции разом восходят или нисходят при повышениях или понижениях.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony differ from each other in this, that paraphony is consonant in an unequal span of time, the notes taking one another up in a certain gentle and apt way, evenly, according to proportions and ratios; whereas antiphony accords in an equal span of time, the high being consonant together with the low, as the eighth with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth, the low, that is, together with the high, or the high with the low, ascending or descending at once in exactly equal proportion, in raisings or in lowerings.

quotes.ru: Парафония и антифония различаются тем, что при парафонии звуки консонируют в неодинаковые промежутки времени, как бы плавно и стройно, равномерно сменяя друг друга сообразно пропорциям и отношениям. Антифония же даёт согласованность в равный промежуток времени, когда высокий звук консонирует с низким одновременно, например восьмой с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым. То есть низкие звуки вместе с высокими, или высокие с низкими, одновременно восходят или нисходят в совершенно равной пропорции при повышениях и понижениях.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony differ in that paraphony is consonant over unequal spans of time, with the notes succeeding one another somewhat smoothly and fittingly, evenly according to proportions and ratios. Antiphony accords over an equal span of time, with a high note consonant simultaneously with a low one, as the eighth with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, and the fifteenth with the eighth. That is, the low notes together with the high, or the high with the low, rise or descend simultaneously in precisely equal proportion as the pitch is raised or lowered.

quotes.ru: Различаются же между собой парафонное и антифонное тем, что парафонное консонирует в неравный промежуток времени, когда звуки как бы мягко и уместно подхватывают друг друга, равномерно, согласно пропорциям и отношениям; антифонное же согласуется в равный промежуток времени, когда высокий [звук] консонирует вместе с низким, как восьмой с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым, — а именно, когда низкие вместе с высокими или высокие с низкими одновременно поднимаются или опускаются в совершенно равной пропорции, при повышениях или понижениях.
quotes.en: The paraphonic and the antiphonic differ from each other in that the paraphonic is consonant in an unequal space of time, the notes taking each other up, as it were, gently and fittingly, evenly, according to proportions and ratios; whereas the antiphonic accords in an equal space of time, the high [note] being consonant together with the low, as the eighth with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, the fifteenth with the eighth; that is, the low notes together with the high, or the high with the low, rising or falling simultaneously in a perfectly equal proportion, in raisings or lowerings.

readings.construal: Preserves inequality for the first span and interprets the second as the same span.

quotes.ru: Парафония отличается от антифонии тем, что при парафонии звуки консонируют в неодинаковые промежутки времени, сменяя друг друга как бы плавно и к месту, с равномерным соблюдением пропорций и отношений. При антифонии же звуки согласуются в один и тот же промежуток времени: высокий звук консонирует одновременно с низким, например восьмой с первым, одиннадцатый с четвёртым, двенадцатый с пятым, пятнадцатый с восьмым. Именно так при повышениях или понижениях низкие звуки вместе с высокими или высокие с низкими одновременно поднимаются или опускаются в совершенно одинаковой пропорции.
quotes.en: Paraphony and antiphony differ in that in paraphony the notes are consonant at unequal intervals of time, taking one another up somewhat gently and fittingly, in even accordance with their proportions and ratios. In antiphony, on the other hand, they agree in the same interval of time, the high note being consonant with the low at the same moment, as the eighth with the first, the eleventh with the fourth, the twelfth with the fifth, and the fifteenth with the eighth. In raisings or lowerings [of pitch] the low notes rise or fall together with the high, or the high with the low, at the same time and in exactly equal proportion.

astra.sense: In paraphony the period is unequal, the notes taking one another up smoothly and fittingly in accordance with their proportions and ratios. In antiphony the period is equal: high sounds with low, as eight with one, eleven with four, twelve with five, fifteen with eight. High and low ascend or descend together in equal proportion as pitch is raised or lowered.

claude.sense: The fourth is made up of two tones and a semitone and, besides, a small part of a tone which, being smaller than the diesis, has no name; the fifth of three tones and a semitone; the octave of six tones; the octave with the fourth of eight tones and a semitone; the octave with the fifth of nine tones and a semitone; twice the octave of twelve tones.

best_ru.why: Exact and complete, keeping the participial 'being smaller than the diesis'; B and D equally correct in shorter sentences.

notes_to_keep.gist: The tone-counting (fourth 2½, fifth 3½, octave 6) is Aristoxenian; the extra 'part of a tone smaller than the diesis' is inconsistent with it (it should reappear in the fifth and octave) and wrong by the ratios: 2½ tones of 9:8 = 509.78 cents exceed 4:3 = 498.04 cents; cf. Sectio canonis props. 14–15 (the octave is less than six tones; the fourth less than two tones and a semitone).
The counts before the increment exceed 4:3, 3:2, 2:1, 8:3, 3:1, 4:1 by 11.73, 11.73, 23.46, 35.19, 35.19, 46.92 cents; Boethius' fourth is two tones and the limma 256:243.

editor_questions: Commentary: say once that the extra 'small part of a tone' contradicts both the Pythagorean ratios and Vinet's own round figures (and V55, where the fourth is two tones and a semitone).

errors.problem: In the Latin the hanging of weights is a separate source of the ratios: after the relative clause has closed on intensione, the semicolon and the repeated ex (aut ... ex ponderum e nervis appensione, parallel to ex dispari ... longitudine and to ex fistularum amplitudine, not to per torsionem inside the relative clause) mark it as a new member of the list. D makes it a second way of producing the tension («при повороте колков или ... при подвешивании»; 'by turning the pegs or ... by hanging weights'). Physically weights do tension a string, so the doctrine is not falsified, but Vinet's point, that the weight experiment is a distinct and better-established method, is lost.

text_issues_review.printed: Inuentæ autem hæ sunt interuallorum / rationes et deprehensæ, ex dispari chor- / datum vel longitudine vel crassitudine: / vel ea, quæ per torsionem clauiculorum / fit, intensione; aut, quod compertum ma- / gis, ex ponderum è neruis appensione: In / iis verò quæ inflata sonant, aut ex fistula- / rum amplitudine, aut ex intensione spiri- / tus ac remissione.
text_issues_review.proposal: (a) 'what is better ascertained'; (b) 'what has rather been found [to be the case]'.
text_issues_review.why: Better ascertained renders the comparative degree of certain knowledge. The weaker 'rather been found to be the case' is possible as a loose paraphrase of comparative preference, but it suppresses what is being compared, namely how securely each procedure established the result. The question of frequency is unexpressed.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. comperio, opening senses [checked] https://alatius.com/ls/index.php?l=comperio

sol.sense: The tetrachord contains the fourth’s capacities, the pentachord the fifth’s, and the octachord the entire force of the octave. The sixteen-string system spans the full double octave, with two sets of capacities: those just listed and those of the octave plus fourth, octave plus fifth, and double octave.

quotes.ru: Из систем же одна — тетрахорд, содержащий все возможности интервала кварты; другая — пентахорд, охватывающий возможности интервала квинты; ещё одна — октахорд, содержащий всю силу интервала октавы; затем ещё одна — шестнадцатиструнная [система], которая объемлет всё напряжение двойной октавы и обладает двоякими возможностями: ведь она содержит в себе и те, о которых мы только что сказали, и возможности интервалов октавы с квартой, октавы с квинтой и двойной октавы.
quotes.en: Of the systems, one is the tetrachord, which contains all the powers of the interval of the fourth; another the pentachord, which embraces the powers of the interval of the fifth; another the octachord, which contains the whole force of the interval of the octave; another, next, the sixteen-stringed [system], comprising the entire tension of the double octave and having twofold powers: for it contains in itself those which we have just mentioned and also the powers of the intervals of the octave and a fourth, the octave and a fifth, and the double octave.

quotes.ru: Из систем же одна — тетрахорд, который содержит все возможности интервала кварты; другая — пентахорд, который охватывает возможности интервала квинты; ещё одна — октахорд, который содержит всю силу интервала октавы; далее ещё одна — шестнадцатиструнная [система], охватывающая всё напряжение двойной октавы и имеющая двойные возможности: ведь она содержит в себе и те, о которых мы только что сказали, и возможности интервалов октавы с квартой, октавы с квинтой и двойной октавы.
quotes.en: Of the systems, one is the tetrachord, which contains all the capacities of the interval of the fourth; another the pentachord, which embraces the capacities of the interval of the fifth; another the octachord, which contains the whole force of the interval of the octave; another, next, the sixteen-string [system], comprising the entire tension of the double octave and having double capacities: for it contains in itself those that we have just mentioned, and the capacities of the intervals of the octave and a fourth, the octave and a fifth, and the double octave.

readings.construal: The whole range in pitch.

quotes.ru: Одна из систем — тетрахорд, вмещающий все возможности интервала кварты. Другая — пентахорд, охватывающий возможности интервала квинты. Ещё одна — октахорд, заключающий в себе всю силу интервала октавы. Далее идёт шестнадцатиструнная система, охватывающая всю высотную протяжённость двойной октавы и обладающая двоякими возможностями: она вмещает как те, о которых мы только что сказали, так и возможности интервалов октавы с квартой, октавы с квинтой и двойной октавы.
quotes.en: One system is the tetrachord, which contains all the capacities of the fourth. Another is the pentachord, which embraces the capacities of the fifth. Another is the octachord, which contains the entire capacity of the octave. Next comes the sixteen-string system, which spans the full pitch range of the double octave and has two kinds of capacity. For it contains both those just mentioned and the capacities of the octave and a fourth, the octave and a fifth, and the double octave.

readings.construal: The full rise from one end of the system to the other.

quotes.ru: Одна из систем — тетрахорд, заключающий в себе все возможности кварты. Другая — пентахорд, охватывающий возможности квинты. Ещё одна — октахорд, вмещающий всю силу октавы. Далее следует шестнадцатиструнная система, охватывающая весь подъём на двойную октаву. Её возможности двояки. Она заключает в себе как только что перечисленные возможности, так и возможности октавы с квартой, октавы с квинтой и двойной октавы.
quotes.en: One of the systems is the tetrachord, which contains all the capacities of the fourth. Another is the pentachord, which embraces the capacities of the fifth. Another is the octachord, which contains the full power of the octave. Next comes the sixteen-string system, which spans the full rise of the double octave and has a twofold capacity. It contains both the capacities we have just described and those of the octave and a fourth, the octave and a fifth, and the double octave.

V52.latin: Harmoniae porro proprium est Systemata illa componere aptareque ad aliquod genus modulationis, ut ad Diatonon, ad Chromaticon, et ad id quod ab ipsa harmonia cognominatum, Harmonicum dicimus.

claude.sense: It is, further, proper to harmony to compose those systems and fit them to some genus of melody (modulatio), as to the diatonic, to the chromatic, and to that which, named after harmony itself, we call harmonic.

notes_to_keep.gist: Diatonon and Chromaticon are Greek neuters (διάτονον, χρωματικόν), later Latin Chromaticum, Diatonum; Harmonicum is the genus modern literature calls enharmonic, rendered 'harmonic' by convention to keep the derivation from harmonia (also D).
modulatio is Vinet's word for melody (Xylander: melodia).

V53.latin: Si igitur tonis plurimum harmonia peragitur, Diatonon sic vocatum efficitur genus: si Hemitoniis, Chromaticum: si vero diesibus fere harmonia continetur, conficitur, quam Harmonicam appellant modulationem.

claude.sense: If, then, harmony is carried through mostly by tones, the genus called Diatonon results; if by semitones, the chromatic; but if harmony is made up almost (for the most part) of dieses, there is produced what they call the harmonic melody (modulatio).

best_ru.why: Exact, keep igitur and the parallel plurimum / fere; D drops igitur.

notes_to_keep.gist: In the tetrachords of V55–V59 two of the three intervals are tones (diatonic), semitones (chromatic), dieses (harmonic): hence 'for the most part'; cf. Theon on the diatonic genus as proceeding mostly by tones (page reference not verified by the reviewer).

sol.sense: Predominant tones yield the diatonic genus, predominant semitones the chromatic, and a preponderance of dieses the melody called harmonic.

text_issues_review.printed: nicum dicimus. Si igitur tonis plurimùm / harmonia peragitur, Diátonon sic voca- / tum efficitur genus: si Hemitoniis, Chro- / maticum: si verò diesibus ferè harmonia / continetur, conficitur, quam Harmonicam / appellant modulationem.
text_issues_review.proposal: (a) 'is for the most part made up of dieses'; (b) 'is held together almost wholly by dieses'.
text_issues_review.why: Fere can mean almost or for the most part. The following omnino makes the almost/entire opposition grammatically possible, but 'almost wholly' implies a stronger numerical or spatial claim than the technical description supports. In V59 two of the three steps are dieses and cover one fifth of the stated compass. 'Chiefly' leaves the basis of predominance implicit.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. fere I–II [checked] https://alatius.com/ls/index.php?l=fere

astra.sense: If harmony proceeds principally by tones the diatonic genus results. With semitones it is the chromatic. If it consists mostly of dieses the resulting melody is called harmonic.

V55.latin: quinimo, quoniam ex tribus intervallis Dia-tessaron intervallum confectum est, duobusque tonis et hemitonio comprehensum, necesse est, postquam duo prima intervalla imposueris, reliquum esse Hemitonium:

claude.sense: nay rather, since the interval Dia-tessaron is made of three intervals and is comprised by two tones and a semitone, it is necessary, once you have put in place the first two intervals, that the remaining one be a semitone:

best_ru.why: Exact; keep quinimo as corrective «напротив»; B («Более того») and D («Ведь», then «Значит») are freer.

notes_to_keep.gist: Here the fourth is exactly two tones and a semitone, without the 'small part' of V39 (also B, D); with exact ratios the remainder after two tones is 256:243 (D).

claude.sense: The diatonic, however, is simple, noble and more natural; therefore Plato too admits it.

best_ru.why: Exact; D brackets [род], equally correct.

best_en.why: Exact.

notes_to_keep.gist: simplum is from the rare simplus, distinct from simplex (Vinet's word for the incomposite intervals, V31); Diatonum beside Diatonon (V52–V56).

Theon gives the same judgement (the diatonic simple, noble, more natural; hence Plato adopts it), with the Timaeus' diatonic division (35b–36b) in view; the Republic (398e–399c) concerns modes, not genera.

sol.sense: The diatonic genus is simple, noble and more natural, which is why Plato also admits it.

best_ru.why: Marks the ellipsis of genus and uses idiomatic predicates.

best_en.why: Both preserve the comparative and Plato’s acceptance.

notes_to_keep.gist: The Timaeus gives a mathematical parallel, and the named modes in the Republic address a different classification. Vinet cites no particular passage.

astra.sense: The diatonic genus is simple, noble and more natural. Accordingly Plato too admits it.

best_en.why: D marks the contextual noun, preserves the comparative and gives et its additive sense before Plato.

notes_to_keep.gist: Distinguish the division in Plato’s Timaeus from the selection of modes in Republic III. Vinet names no dialogue.

divergences.verdict: «пеан, гименей» / 'paean, hymenaeus' are established words, so describing the hymenaeus (D) is unnecessary though not wrong. For Exodius there is no established modern term: either the transliteration with a note (A, C) or a plain description (B) is within about.md § 4.1. B's 'exit/closing song' matches the dictionaries: LSJ gives ἐξόδιος 'of or belonging to an exit', τὸ ἐξόδιον 'finale of a tragedy', and Latin exodium 'after-piece', transferred 'conclusion, end'. D's «прощальная песнь» ('farewell song') narrows the sense toward leave-taking. LSJ records no funeral sense for ἐξόδιος (only 'departure, death' for ἔξοδος); D's funerary alternative (in its doubt) rests on later Byzantine liturgical usage, which the Latin does not suggest. The choice between A/C and B is the editor's.

Non enim sola interuallorum mu- / tatione, neque sola eorum differentia: sed / etiam lentioribus, et concitatis transitio- / nibus, pausis quoqne et fluxibus, atque va- / riis tactibus pulsibúsque, pro vario manus / temperamento, infinitæ et diuersæ mo- / dulationes conficiuntur.
